purpose: This vaccine helps protect you and your children from measles, a serious and very contagious viral infection. Measles can cause high fever, rash, and in some cases dangerous complications like pneumonia or brain swelling. Getting vaccinated is one of the best ways to keep yourself and those around you safe from this disease.
how_it_works: The vaccine contains a very weak, live form of the measles virus that cannot make you sick. When it is injected, your immune system recognizes it as a threat and builds up protective antibodies. If you are ever exposed to the real measles virus in the future, your immune system is already trained to fight it off quickly.
common_side_effects: After getting the shot, you might notice soreness, redness, or swelling where the needle went in. Some people get a mild fever or a faint rash about 1 to 2 weeks later. These reactions are normal and usually go away on their own within a few days.
warnings: Do not get this vaccine if you are pregnant, have a weakened immune system, or are allergic to gelatin or neomycin. Tell your doctor if you have recently received blood products or other vaccines. In rare cases, serious allergic reactions can occur, so you will be asked to wait at the clinic for about 15 minutes after your shot.
typical_dosing: Children usually get two doses: the first at 12 to 15 months of age, and the second between 4 and 6 years old. Adults who were never vaccinated or never had measles may also need one or two doses. Your doctor will let you know what is right for your situation.
